vectors.carrier: A sound review begins by considering the balance of material together with immediate threats before comparing plans in greater detail. The safety of the king deserves close attention because exposed squares can make quiet choices less dependable than they first appear. Loose pieces should be identified before a continuation is examined because a series of exchanges can change their protection in an important way. Possible pawn breaks need to be compared with the resulting structure in mind instead of being judged solely by their immediate activity at the moment of contact. The progress of development remains important when multiple plans look plausible because an inactive piece can restrict coordination throughout the position. A sensible candidate list includes active ideas and quieter improvements so the comparison does not depend on a single attractive impression. Concrete forcing lines deserve concrete calculation covering checks and captures considered before quiet replies whenever the position makes that ordering relevant. The opponent's resources merit equally careful attention since an attractive idea can be undermined by an accurate response that the first review missed. Less direct alternatives can prove useful if immediate action would leave weaknesses without obtaining a clear compensating benefit. Exchanges call for evaluation by the position they leave alongside the activity of the pieces that remain after the sequence ends. Confidence in an assessment should reflect the evidence rather than the fluency of the explanation when the critical details remain insufficiently checked. A clear conclusion must connect the candidate with its concrete purpose and identify the principal tradeoff that remains to be assessed. A concluding review should recheck assumptions and separate established facts from reasonable expectations before stating the assessment as a finished argument.
